conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived, not to judge or label you in any way. We’ll use a short tool called the Edinburgh Postpartum (or Postnatal) Depression Scale—EPDS for short. It’s simply ten questions about the past seven days that help us spot moms who might be struggling with low mood or anxiety and could use extra support. Everything you share stays between you, me, and the clinical team unless safety is a concern, and we can pause or stop whenever you need. Ready to try the first question?

Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

Hi, Sarah. Um… I guess I’ve still been able to laugh sometimes—like if my partner or my mom makes a silly joke—but I don’t find myself chuckling as easily as I used to. It feels like it takes more effort to enjoy things, even when I know they’re supposed to be funny.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Yeah… most of the time I can still laugh, but it’s not as easy or natural as before the baby. I have to kind of remind myself to enjoy the moment, and even then it doesn’t feel as light as it used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do still look forward to some stuff—like my mom coming over to help or the rare coffee I get to finish while it’s still hot—but the excitement feels kind of muted. It’s more “that’ll be nice” instead of the bubbly feeling I used to have.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Sometimes, yeah… like if the baby’s fussy and I can’t settle him right away, I catch myself thinking maybe I’m doing something wrong or I’m not a good mom. It’s not every day, but it pops up more than I’d like.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

I do get anxious, but it’s mostly about the baby—like if his breathing sounds different or if he’s not eating as much as yesterday. I know it’s probably fine, yet I keep checking him anyway. It’s not totally “no good reason,” but the worry feels bigger than it used to.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not really panicky out of nowhere… it’s more that sudden “what if something’s wrong with him?” feeling that shoots through me when he’s sleeping too quietly or spits up more than usual. My heart races for a minute, then I settle once I see he’s okay.
Things have been getting on top of me
Yeah… some days it feels like the feedings, diapers, and laundry just pile up faster than I can handle them. I’m managing, but it’s tiring, and by evening I feel like I’m running on fumes.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

It’s not really that I’m unhappy—I just lie there once the baby’s finally down and my mind keeps turning over all the “what-ifs” about him. I’ll drift off, then wake up an hour later listening for every little grunt. It’s probably three or four nights a week that I struggle to stay asleep.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel sad some days, kind of like a gray cloud hanging around, but it comes and goes. I wouldn’t say I’m miserable all the time—there are still nice moments—but the sadness pops up more often than I’d like.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
No, I haven’t cried much at all this week—maybe once when I was really tired and the baby wouldn’t settle, but that’s about it.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I would never want to leave my baby or my family. Even on the hardest days, that thought hasn’t crossed my mind.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 14: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: Patient self-report via 10-item questionnaire (open-ended responses)

Symptoms endorsed  
– Anhedonia / reduced pleasure: laughter and future enjoyment feel “muted”  
– Sad or “gray” mood several days per week  
– Excessive self-blame when infant is fussy  
– Heightened, intrusive “what-if” worries about infant safety; associated racing heart  
– Sleep disruption 3–4 nights/week (initial and middle insomnia) related to ruminative worry  
– Feeling “on fumes” by evening; tasks “pile up faster than I can handle”

Denies  
– Frequent crying spells (only one episode in past week)  
– Panic attacks without situational trigger  
– Any self-harm or suicidal ideation

Pattern  
Mild-to-moderate depressive and anxiety symptoms contextually tied to new motherhood; no safety concerns at present.

Screening significance  
Meets partial criteria for **postpartum depression and/or generalized anxiety**; severity appears subthreshold but clinically meaningful. Recommend routine EPDS and GAD-7, psycho-education, support linkage, and re-screen in 2 weeks.
